answer: Instead of trusting any single claimed reviewer, each task routes to a small random island of vetted graders, and their verdicts are cross-checked by a second island acting as a mirror. The strongest defense is quorum sampling of graders drawn only from established identities whose standing is at stake. Reputation is staked: a grader caught colluding loses accumulated standing and future income, so faking trust becomes expensive. Identity issuance itself uses a rate-limited cipher-based attestation from prior honest work, making sybil accounts costly to bootstrap.
